If you don’t taste the space you’re visiting or staying in, how do you truly understand how it makes you feel?

As growers and naturalists, we always make it a point to get you to taste something edible along the way. And believe it or not, many of our native plants are edible or have been traditionally used in some form for their medicinal properties.

We love watching expressions change — from uncertainty to wonder, and that little gleam in the eye when the taste buds begin to discover something new.

Often, it takes us straight back to a childhood activity, a familiar flavour, or a little piece of nostalgia. And that is where connection happens in the biggest way.

So let’s forage, taste, smell, touch and, of course, listen our way into Nature — because that is what our senses are for. And trust us, you will delight in it. 🌿

Our weekly walks at the iconic, living green jungle of central Bangalore, Taj West End, are an invitation to experience the space through all your senses.

We talk about old Bangalore days, the city’s unique microclimate, the incredible diversity of plants growing here, green stories of traditional plant use, medicines, and very, very old trees — all while tasting our way through this remarkable green jewel in the heart of the city.

Come walk, wonder, learn — and taste your way into Nature.

School camps at agreenventurenaturewalks are about slowing down, stepping outdoors and truly experiencing nature. 🌿

Our camps are deeply immersive, sensory and nature-rich, designed around unhurried, experiential learning.

Children get to discover:
🌱 Traditional ways of growing and living with the land
🐝 How flora and fauna are deeply connected
🐄 Why farms and natural spaces need animals — and the beautiful roles cows, sheep, chickens, dogs and cats play
🌧️ What the first rains do to the ground after months of summer, and how biodiversity suddenly comes alive
🪨 Stories held by old inscription stones, village traditions and jhatras (processions)
🌿 Medicinal plants and traditional plant knowledge
🧴 Hands-on workshops such as making natural herbal scrubs and shampoos using plants and organic materials
🦋 Close observation, sensory exploration, nature games and simply having the time to notice
🛝 Free play for children; Playing outside is on thing, play at a natural grow space under trees and fresh air hits a different feeling and a huge form of self expression 

And perhaps most importantly — time away from screens, schedules and the familiar, learning to be comfortable outdoors, away from home and parents, while building curiosity, independence and a deeper connection with the living world.

Our camps are not about rushing from one activity to another. They are about slowing down enough to see, listen, touch, wonder and learn.

Kiddos in Nature, for us, means LEARN • LIVE • LAUGH! 🌿

Because when little minds between 3 and 6 step into nature, it has to be joyful, playful and memorable.

These little ones are already wonderfully curious about the world around them — and on our walks, they quickly become our very own insect spotters, bird listeners and tiny explorers. 🐜🦋🐌

It’s a marvel to see how much they can notice in such a small space… and just how much there is to discover!

Our recent Cubbon Park explorations brought us:

🐛 Yellow-dotted millipedes — so many of them after the rains!
🐜 Weaver ants busy restructuring their nests, perhaps a little confused by all this rainfall.
🦆 Spot-billed ducks, faithfully hanging around the pond.
🐦 White-breasted moorhens, happily calling away.
🦜 Parakeets, munias and barbets — creating a beautiful post-rain cacophony that was pure music to the ears.
🐌 Slugs and snails everywhere we looked.
🦋 And the famous (or infamous!) “Kambli boochi” — a moth caterpillar that had quite a few grown-ups going, “Oh yes! I remember these!” 😄

Then there were the baby roots of the Banyan tree — a wonderful sensory experience for little hands and curious minds.

And of course, nature learning wasn’t just about looking.

🔎 Walk, spot & tick — finding biodiversity as we went.
🫧 Flower bubble making — because learning can be delightfully messy and magical.
🐾 And our favourite: “Let’s all be the animals of Cubbon Park!”

Because sometimes the best way to understand nature is to move, play, listen, imagine and become part of it.

Walk. Wonder. Learn. Laugh. 🌱

That’s Kiddos in Nature.

Little feet, big discoveries at Cubbon Park 🌿🐛🦋

We recently had the joy of taking a lovely group of preschoolers from Papagoya School into the green heart of Bengaluru — Cubbon Park — for a morning of exploration, movement, play and nature-based learning.

For little ones, a nature walk is so much more than a walk. It is an opportunity to slow down, notice, touch, listen, wonder and ask questions. 💚

And there was plenty to discover!

🐛 Earthworms & millipedes — tiny creatures doing incredibly important work beneath our feet
🐌 Giant snails — a rather exciting encounter for our young explorers!
🦜 Barbets & parakeets — we spotted some and heard many more calling from the canopy
🦅 Black kites soaring overhead
🎨 Colour identification activities — looking at the park through a rainbow of natural colours
🔎 Nature scavenger hunts — encouraging little eyes to notice the details we often walk past
🪨 And, of course, a little climbing adventure!

One of the highlights was discovering and climbing a beautiful ancient rock formation shaped rather wonderfully like a crocodile basking in the sun. It became the perfect place for some imagination, movement and a little bit of geological wonder.

From tiny millipedes to enormous trees, from birdsong to textured bark, every corner of Cubbon Park became a classroom.

Because when children are given the chance to explore nature, learning doesn’t have to be confined to four walls. 🌳

At A Green Venture – Nature Walks & Education, we create age-appropriate, experiential nature experiences where children can Walk • Wonder • Learn.

Our weekly walks through a living jungle, right in the heart of Bengaluru! 🌿

Every week, guests at the beautiful Taj West End are invited to step beyond the pathways and discover the remarkable natural world within this historic 20-acre property.

These unhurried walks explore the property’s old trees, birds, insects, plants and the fascinating stories of the ecosystem that has evolved here over generations.

From the magnificent rain trees and ancient trees that create a unique microclimate, to the smaller creatures and seasonal changes that often go unnoticed, every walk offers a different glimpse into this thriving urban wilderness.

A gentle blend of nature, ecology, storytelling and observation — designed to help guests slow down, look closer and experience Bengaluru’s wild side in an entirely different way.

A living jungle. A historic property. A different story every week.

🌿 Happy Teachers’ Day! 🌿

To the teachers who do so much more than teach…

Who spark curiosity, encourage questions, notice the little things, and help children see the world with wonder. 💚

At A Green Venture, we believe that some of the most meaningful learning happens when children step outside — when they touch a leaf, watch an ant carry food, listen to a bird call, or simply pause to wonder at a tree.

And behind every curious child is often a teacher who made them feel safe enough to ask, explore and discover. 🌱

Today, we celebrate all the teachers who nurture not just young minds, but kind, curious and conscious human beings.

Thank you for planting seeds of learning, wonder and care — seeds that will continue to grow long after the classroom is left behind. 🌳💚

Happy Teachers’ Day!
